title: fix(ui): allow owned-session appearance and retain linked accounts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes owned-session appearance controls being denied or silently ignored for scoped session writers, and existing Discord links being hidden by an available but unlinked account.

## User Impact

Users with session-write access can set or reset icon/color on their own sessions from the sidebar, Chat header, and Sessions page. Profile initially presents an existing Discord link even when that account cannot start new linking, while retaining an explicit account choice during status refresh. No new permissions, stored preference, migration, or user action is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

All three appearance dispatchers now use the existing own-session admission contract and captured session identity. Initial account selection prefers linked accounts, then available accounts. Cross-user, reader, Home, communication, and server authority restrictions are unchanged.

The production delta is +23/-11 lines. The +547 net test lines cover three distinct UI dispatchers, captured-identity and denied-access contracts, retained-account selection, and actual built browser consumers. The per-change allocation grants only the 147 lines above the default 400; no global budget or baseline was changed. Consolidating away a dispatcher or browser case would leave the original silent-action failure untested.

## Evidence

- Initial owner regressions reproduced 5 failures; correction regressions reproduced all seven missing dispatcher/linked-account cases. Focused repaired cases and independent review closed those findings.
- Independent proof: 68 UI/shared-scope and 25 Gateway authority/identity tests passed on unchanged production. Worker focused proof covered 89 distinct cases across scoped runs.
- Real Chromium, freshly built UI, synthetic Gateway: scoped writer passed (21.461s), reader passed (6.635s), linked-unavailable/explicit-selection Profile case passed (4.136s), across separate focused runs. Browser writer requires exactly 17 own-key patches, including nine captured-ID appearance writes; it verifies reopened state and reset on all three surfaces. Negative attempts and forbidden RPC assertions remain.
- Scoped production/test typechecks, lint, formatting, commit hooks and full-range test-line ratchet passed. Browser build/run wall time for the final writer command was 48.85s. Hosted CI duration will be available in checks.
- Follow-up readiness repair: await in-flight lazy branch-action imports before the existing Create PR assertion, without changing its assertions, timeout, or callbacks. With a controlled 1,100 ms real Vite transform delay, the original case failed and the corrected cases passed 2/2; the final uninstrumented file passed 20/20. Focused lint, format, UI-chat test typecheck and full-range +547/400+147 ratchet passed. Independent exact-delta review found no P0–P2 issues. This diagnoses a real readiness defect; it does not claim a matching baseline CI failure or that import delay was the sole cause of the earlier hosted failure. Fresh-head CI remains required.
- Independent source review approved behavior. Local AutoReview fallback was used because the preferred reviewer executable was unavailable; its refresh-timing advisory was rejected after inspecting the existing loading/disabled-Connect contract. No unresolved behavior finding remains.

The screenshots below are inspected, synthetic before/after user actions on the corrected build, not historical pre-fix or deployed guest acceptance. They show all three appearance surfaces and the Profile account choice. No real Discord OAuth, live deployment, or cross-device persistence was tested. These limitations do not change the retained server-authority checks.
